children: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi is expected to keep her finance minister, Satsuki Katayama, in her job in a cabinet reshuffle expected later this month, the Mainichi newspaper reported on Friday.
A former finance ministry bureaucrat, Katayama has played a key role negotiating with U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on a rare joint U.S.-Japan yen intervention in late July.
